title: spec review: B4b v6 (fix round of T-1491): execute result derived from git state WITHOUT auto-commit; inputs pinned at the claim, one guarded writer for done, held AND the fallback failed write, whole derivation guarded, goal id as the outcome parent
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label B4b-v6. Respec of B4b v5 T-1546 (superseded; spec review request_changes 2026-10-02 10:55). Still a fix round of T-1491 (constraints.fix_round_for), so its merge stamps T-1491 and B7 T-1494 / B5 T-1554 become ready; cuts from goal/T-1403. This text is the whole contract. The commit-now resume stays DROPPED; auto-commit of leftovers stays PARKED as B4c.

Contract from B4a (MERGED): gitutil.head_sha(worktree, timeout=60) -> sha | None (gitutil.py:30) and gitutil.execute_outcome(worktree, parent, scope, *, since=None) -> {ahead, head, dirty_in_scope, dirty_out_of_scope} | None (gitutil.py:40-56). parent is the GOAL ID, not a branch: _resolve_base(worktree, parent) builds f"goal/{parent}" then falls back to origin/main and main (gitutil.py:36-42). 'ahead' is `git rev-list --count {since or base}..HEAD`, so with since=pre_head it counts only commits after the pre-run head. None for a missing worktree or a HEAD change during the reads. Hold prefix 'execute_incomplete' (B5 maps it to failure kind 'incomplete').

Facts (scout T-1539 plus Planner grep, goal/T-1403 = 5c4ba3d, provenance repo):
G1 spawn.run_worker (spawn.py:1513-1611): t = dict(bus.get(task_id)) BEFORE the claim and never refreshed. Locals before run_claude: pool, t, role, epoch = t['_launch_epoch'], acct, model = pool.cfg['models'][t['tier']], prompt, allowlist, budget, timeout; for execute t['executor'] = f'claude:{tier}' (1564). The claim line is `bus.claim(task_id, f'claude:{acct.id}', str(ensure_worktree(task_id)))` (1603) and discards the path; t.get('worktree') is None on a fresh launch. The worktree path is Path(ensure_worktree(task_id)) (idempotent, = ROOT/'wt'/task_id); the scope is t['scope']; the goal id is t['parent']. run_claude calls: `first = run_claude(pool, acct, t, prompt, model, allowlist, budget, timeout)` (1611) and a second call in the escalation branch (1633).
G2 Resume path: resume_worker (1755-1759, from worker_control.steer at 283) sets prompt = resume_prompt, t['_resume_session'], model and tools from worker_registry.get; it skips packet/render, pool.reserve, bus.claim and ensure_worktree; run_claude still upserts the registry 'starting' and passes --resume; the result goes through the same status branches.
G3 Tool escalation (1614-1635): needs disclosure_mode == 'active', a _hidden_tool_request and no pipeline.tool_escalation_used; it writes status running and result None, then replaces r with a second run_claude; the first result is kept only for _combined_usage; nothing touches git between the calls.
G4 Non-JSON: run_claude calls worker_registry.finish(task_id, 'failed', 'non_json', epoch=epoch) (1381-1383) and returns {'status': 'failed', 'reason': f'non-JSON output (rc={rc}): {text[-500:]}'}, only those two keys (every recorded case is rc=143 with empty text: SIGTERM). run_worker's failed branch today: worker_control.write_if_current(task_id, epoch, bus.update, task_id, status='failed', reason=r['reason']) (1711-1716); resume_hint.partial_output only when r['output']['result'] is a str, so never for non-JSON.
G5 Done path (1655-1660): posted = fit_result({'summary': r['output'].get('result', '')[:3000], 'executed_by': f"claude:{t['tier']}", 'review': 'other account, different model; label PR same-family-review'}); posted = contracts.process(task_id, role, posted, cfg=pool.cfg, session=repair_session); write_if_current(task_id, epoch, bus.post_result, task_id, posted, 'done'). No commit or derived_from key today.
G6 run_worker ends with `return r` (1723) after the finally that calls worker_control.release_if_current(task_id, epoch, pool, release_usage or r or {}). Consumers: daemon.py:1011,1085,1305,1671,1690 and mcp.py:61 run it in threads and discard the value; executor.run_fallback (643-665) discards it; spawn.resume_worker returns it to worker_control.steer (283), which does not branch on status.
G7 worker_control (imports `from . import bus, evidence, pool, worker_registry`, line 9, so bus.locked is reached through the module attribute): write_if_current(task_id, epoch, method, *args, **fields) holds bus.locked() and calls method only when is_current (137-171); is_current(task_id, epoch) is epoch >= pipeline.steer_epoch (default 1; read at 204, written by steer at 272); release_if_current at 207; cancel() emits the registry event 'cancel_requested' (status cancelling), terminates the pid, then under the lock does bus.update(status='held', hold_reason='cancelled', pid=None, result=bounded partial), a pool release and worker_registry.finish(task_id, 'cancelled'); it does not change the epoch.
G8 bus.locked() (bus.py:20-41) is reentrant per thread through a depth counter (bus._held.depth): nested bus.post_result / bus.update inside a locked block do not take the flock again.
G9 worker_registry.finish(task_id, status, reason=None, *, epoch=None) (worker_registry.py:186-199): terminal statuses only; under bus.locked(); no write when epoch < the doc epoch or when the doc status is cancelling/cancelled and status != 'cancelled'; 'held' emits a 'held' event then an 'exit' event. worker_registry.upsert(task_id, **fields) (111) takes bus.locked() itself (113) and writes allowed fields including status_reason; worker_registry.get(task_id) (123) takes no lock. worker_registry.reconcile touches only active (non-terminal) entries.
G10 contracts.process(task_id, role, result, *, cfg=None, session=None, thread=None, preserve=False) (contracts.py:158-184) returns the input unchanged when the contracts mode is off or the role has no schema; otherwise validates, repairs, writes a decision_log 'output_contract' row and returns recovered['result'] when active-mode recovery ran, else the input; unknown-key survival is not pinned, so the derived keys are re-attached after it. spawn.fit_result(result, cap=bus.MAX_RESULT_CHARS) (1476) returns the input unchanged when it fits, else a dict copy with summary[:1500] and list values trimmed.
G11 bus.post_result(tid, result, status='done') (bus.py:212-219) raises ValueError above MAX_RESULT_CHARS (6000), sets confidence/provenance defaults and calls update(tid, status=status, result=result); it does not clear hold_reason. bus.claim (bus.py:209) sets status running, assigned_to, worktree, claimed_at and does NOT clear result, so a re-claimed fix round or re-launch still carries the earlier round's result. bus.log_run(*, attempt=1, **fields) (359) accepts arbitrary keyword fields; the existing run_worker log_run calls pass no attempt.
G12 run_claude never writes the bus task status (inside it: worker_registry.upsert/event and bus.update(pid=, account=, packet_meta=, pipeline=) only); the escalation branch writes status running explicitly; the non-JSON finish touches the registry only. So the task is still 'running' when derivation runs.
G13 No code outside worker_registry.py reads status_reason 'non_json' (grep: daemon.py, failures.py, scorecard.py, mcp.py, cli.py, executor.py have no hits).
G14 Test seams in tests/test_spawn.py: patch.object(spawn, 'run_claude', side_effect=fn), patch.object(spawn, 'ensure_worktree', return_value=path), patch.object(spawn, 'worker_registry'), patch.object(spawn, 'Pool', return_value=pool); imports `from orchestrator import bus, pool as P, spawn` with _harness TMP and scratch_repo.

Change:
1. Seams. `from . import gitutil` joins spawn.py's package imports; module attributes `execute_outcome = gitutil.execute_outcome` and `head_sha = gitutil.head_sha` are what run_worker calls (patchable by name). derive = pool.cfg.get('spawn', {}).get('derive_execute_result', False): DEFAULT FALSE until B5 (T-1554) maps execute_incomplete holds; the flip is a one-line follow-up. False means today's behaviour exactly; head_sha is never called.
2. Claim refactor and inputs pinned. The claim line becomes `wt = Path(ensure_worktree(task_id))` then `bus.claim(task_id, f'claude:{acct.id}', str(wt))` for every role, so ensure_worktree runs exactly once per launch. Directly after the claim, only when role == 'execute' and derive and resume_task is None: goal_id = t.get('parent'); scope = list(t.get('scope') or []); pre_head = head_sha(wt) inside try/except -> None. The head is read at the claim for EVERY such launch, before the outcome is known (it must precede the run); on the resume path and for other roles none of this runs (G2). Because pre_head is read at THIS launch's claim, commits from earlier rounds in a reused worktree are never counted.
3. worker_control.cancel_or_steer_pending(task_id, epoch) -> bool: True when worker_registry.get(task_id) has status in {'cancelling', 'cancelled', 'steering'}, or bus.get(task_id) is held with hold_reason 'cancelled', or not is_current(task_id, epoch); False otherwise; never raises (missing registry entry -> False).
4. Trigger. After the final r is known (after the escalation branch, so only the final run_claude result counts; since = pre_head spans both runs on purpose: the first run's commits are the task's work), derivation runs only when role == 'execute' and derive and resume_task is None and pre_head is not None and r['status'] == 'failed' and str(r.get('reason', '')).startswith('non-JSON output') and not cancel_or_steer_pending(task_id, epoch). Every other outcome keeps today's write; the done path never calls execute_outcome.
5. Whole derivation guarded. Items 6-8 run inside ONE try/except Exception. On any exception (execute_outcome, fit_result, contracts.process, size check, post_if_current) run_worker logs through the existing notify path and falls back to item 9 with reason r['reason'] + ' (derivation failed: <exception class name>)'. o = execute_outcome(wt, goal_id, scope, since=pre_head); None -> item 9 with the original reason.
6. Decision (no git mutation anywhere). (i) o['ahead'] == 0 -> payload {'hold_reason': 'execute_incomplete: no commits', 'resume_hint': {'partial_output': r['reason'], 'dirty_in_scope': o['dirty_in_scope'], 'dirty_out_of_scope': o['dirty_out_of_scope'], 'head': o['head']}} posted with status 'held'; (ii) o['dirty_in_scope'] or o['dirty_out_of_scope'] -> the same shape with hold_reason 'execute_incomplete: uncommitted changes'; (iii) ahead > 0 and clean -> candidate = {'summary': 'derived from git state after ' + r['reason'][:300], 'commit': o['head'], 'executed_by': t['executor'], 'derived_from': 'git_state', 'review': 'derived from git state; other account, different model; label PR same-family-review'}; fitted = fit_result(candidate); processed = dict(contracts.process(task_id, role, fitted, cfg=pool.cfg, session=None)); processed.update({k: candidate[k] for k in ('commit', 'derived_from', 'executed_by', 'review')}); processed.setdefault('confidence', 0.0); processed.setdefault('provenance', ['repo']); if len(json.dumps(processed)) > bus.MAX_RESULT_CHARS -> item 9; else post_if_current(task_id, epoch, 'done', processed). Documented in the run_worker docstring: rc=143 may be a timeout, a reaper kill or an external kill that never went through cancel(), so 'ahead > 0 and clean' can post a half-finished run as done; this is intentional: the since-relative ahead count, the tests-green gate (acceptance-named tests present and green) and the derived markers (summary, derived_from, review text) are the backstops.
7. ONE guarded writer for every outcome: worker_control.post_if_current(task_id, epoch, status, payload) -> bool, status in {'done', 'held', 'failed'}. payload keys are validated BEFORE the lock ('held' needs hold_reason and resume_hint; 'failed' needs reason; 'done' needs summary; KeyError otherwise, raised outside the lock). Exactly one outermost `bus.locked()` entry (G7, G8). Inside: fresh = bus.get(task_id); entry = worker_registry.get(task_id) or {}; return False and write nothing unless fresh['status'] == 'running' (G12) and is_current(task_id, epoch) and entry.get('status') not in {'cancelling', 'cancelled', 'steering'}. There is NO check of the existing result's commit (G11: claim never clears result, so that check would refuse every re-claimed fix round and stall it in running). Otherwise ONE bus.update per status, still inside the lock: 'done' -> bus.update(task_id, status='done', result=payload, hold_reason=None); 'held' -> bus.update(task_id, status='held', hold_reason=payload['hold_reason'], resume_hint=payload['resume_hint']); 'failed' -> bus.update(task_id, status='failed', reason=payload['reason']); then worker_registry.upsert(task_id, status_reason='derived_done' | 'execute_incomplete' | 'non_json' respectively) (the registry status stays the terminal 'failed' that finish wrote; G13: nothing reads non_json and reconcile skips terminal entries, so the task is never re-handled; docstring); return True.
8. Bookkeeping after a derived write returned True: bus.log_run(task=task_id, role='execute', outcome='derived_done' | 'execute_incomplete', executor=t['executor'], tier=t['tier'], account=acct.id, derived_from='git_state') exactly once (no attempt argument, like the existing calls); r is replaced by {'status': 'done' | 'held', 'derived_from': 'git_state', 'reason': <original reason>} before `return r` (G6: no consumer branches on it; the finally still releases).
9. Fallback failed write, also guarded: whenever derivation does not write (trigger false but derive on, outcome None, exception, size, or post_if_current returned False for a derived outcome), run_worker calls post_if_current(task_id, epoch, 'failed', {'reason': <reason>}) instead of today's write_if_current. True -> r stays the failed dict (reason possibly suffixed per item 5) and no derived log_run entry. False -> somebody else wrote (status no longer running, stale epoch, or cancel/steer in flight): run_worker returns {'status': 'superseded', 'reason': <reason>} with no write and no log_run; the registry entry stays failed/non_json on purpose; the output_contract decision_log row written for an unposted candidate is accepted (docstring). So every path ends with the task done, held or failed, never running with a terminal registry entry. With derive False (the default) the non-JSON path is byte-for-byte today's: write_if_current(bus.update, status='failed', reason=...).
10. Key passthrough is unconditional (item 6), so contracts.py needs no read and no change.

Tests (SPEC RULE): tests/test_spawn.py::test_failed_without_reason_key_sets_default_and_resume_hint passes unchanged. Cases (a)-(c) of the first acceptance test use a REAL scratch_repo worktree returned by the ensure_worktree patch (head_sha and execute_outcome unpatched) so the since-relative ahead count is exercised; the spawn.execute_outcome / spawn.head_sha seams are patched only for the 'raises' and 'returns None' cases; both patched only in the new derivation TestCase's setUp, never in every execute TestCase; derive defaults to False so legacy tests never reach them. Cancel/steer signals: registry status through worker_registry.upsert; steer by bumping pipeline.steer_epoch; pre-posted done/held/failed through bus.update or bus.post_result before derivation runs. The lock-entry counter replaces bus.locked with a wrapper that counts only entries made at bus._held.depth == 0 (G8). The registry fixture for the 'status stays failed' assertion pre-creates the entry at status 'failed', status_reason 'non_json' through worker_registry.upsert.

Out of scope: gitutil.py, daemon.py, executor.py, failures.py, contracts.py, worker_registry.py, pool.toml. Rollback: `git revert` of the merge, or [spawn].derive_execute_result = false (the default). Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run tests/test_spawn.py tests/test_worker_control.py in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by line number. Every test named in the acceptance must exist in the diff; the gate checks for them by id.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_execute_result_derived_from_git_state: passes: with derive_execute_result True and run_claude returning {'status': 'failed', 'reason': 'non-JSON output (rc=143): '} (no output key) for an execute task on a fresh launch (ensure_worktree patched to a real scratch git worktree and called exactly once, t['worktree'] None, execute_outcome and head_sha unpatched): (a) when the run added a commit and the tree is clean, the task is posted done in one bus.update with result.commit == the worktree HEAD, derived_from 'git_state', executed_by == t['executor'], summary starting 'derived from git state after ', review text starting 'derived from git state', hold_reason None, bus.log_run called exactly once with outcome 'derived_done' and no attempt argument, the registry entry status 'failed' with status_reason 'derived_done', and run_worker returns {'status': 'done', 'derived_from': 'git_state', ...}; (b) with any uncommitted path, in scope or out, the task is held 'execute_incomplete: uncommitted changes' through post_if_current with resume_hint.dirty_in_scope/dirty_out_of_scope/head and partial_output == the reason text, git status unchanged, registry status_reason 'execute_incomplete', run_worker returns status 'held'; (c) with one commit made before the claim and none after, the task is held 'execute_incomplete: no commits' (the ahead count is since-relative); (d) a run_claude 'done' result never calls execute_outcome, while head_sha was called exactly once, at the claim

tests/test_spawn.py::test_derivation_falls_back_to_guarded_failed_write_or_superseded: passes: the task ends failed with the reason kept (no derived log_run entry, registry stays failed/non_json) when derive_execute_result is False (head_sha never called, written through write_if_current exactly as today), when the failed reason does not start with 'non-JSON output', when head_sha returns None, when execute_outcome returns None or raises (reason suffixed ' (derivation failed: RuntimeError)' in the raising case), when contracts.process raises, and when the registry status is 'cancelling', 'cancelled' or 'steering' or pipeline.steer_epoch was bumped (in those four cases nothing is written and run_worker returns status 'superseded'); a task already held 'cancelled' is left untouched; a re-claimed task whose earlier result already carries a commit is still derived (the existing-commit guard is gone); resume_worker with derive True never calls head_sha; in the tool-escalation case derivation uses the final run_claude result with since equal to the head read before the first run; when the worker already posted done, held or failed before derivation, post_if_current returns False for the done, both holds AND the fallback failed write, nothing is written, run_worker returns {'status': 'superseded', ...}; in every case the task is never left in status running

tests/test_worker_control.py::test_post_if_current_single_lock_entry: passes: worker_control.post_if_current(task_id, epoch, status, payload) raises KeyError outside the lock for a 'held' payload without hold_reason or resume_hint and for a 'failed' payload without reason; makes exactly one outermost bus.locked entry (bus.locked replaced by a wrapper counting entries at bus._held.depth == 0), re-reads the task and the registry inside the lock, returns False and writes nothing when is_current is False, when the fresh status is 'done', 'held' or 'failed', or when the registry status is cancelling, cancelled or steering; an existing result with a commit does not block; otherwise performs exactly one bus.update (done: status, result and hold_reason None; held: status, hold_reason, resume_hint; failed: status and reason), sets the registry status_reason to 'derived_done', 'execute_incomplete' or 'non_json' while the registry status stays 'failed', and returns True

tests/test_worker_control.py::test_cancel_or_steer_pending_matrix: passes: cancel_or_steer_pending returns True for registry status cancelling, cancelled and steering, for a task held 'cancelled' and for a stale epoch, False for a running task with a current epoch and a registry entry in 'running', and False without raising for a missing registry entry

risks.issue: rc=143 can come from a timeout, a reaper kill or an external kill. 'ahead > 0 and clean' then posts a half-finished run as done. The spec admits this and relies on the tests-green gate and derived markers. A reviewer may still object, because the gate only checks that the acceptance-named tests exist and pass, not that the work is complete. The risk is contained because derive_execute_result defaults to False.

post_if_current writes done with a raw bus.update. That skips bus.post_result's MAX_RESULT_CHARS check and its confidence/provenance defaults. Those are only re-implemented in the spawn.py caller, so another caller of post_if_current could write an oversize or default-less result. The 'done' payload check in the writer covers only the summary key.

The 'done' write passes hold_reason=None to bus.update. The spec does not confirm that bus.update treats None as 'clear' and not 'leave unchanged'. If it skips None values, a task that was previously held would keep its stale hold_reason after a derived done.
If head_sha raises or returns None at the claim, derivation is skipped without any log. Every such failure then silently becomes the plain failed write, so a broken git read is invisible.

The cancel_or_steer_pending pre-check duplicates the checks post_if_current makes under the lock. It is TOCTOU-prone and adds a second source of truth for the same condition. It is harmless, but the matrix test pins it.

The log_run assertion 'exactly once, no attempt' assumes run_worker makes no other log_run call on the failed or derived path. The spec does not state this. A pre-existing log_run in the failed branch would break test (a).

suggested_spec_changes: Have post_if_current's 'done' branch enforce the size limit and the confidence/provenance defaults itself, raising ValueError before the lock. Alternatively, call bus.post_result inside the lock, which G8 allows and which is still one update. Then no caller can bypass them.
Add an assertion that bus.update(hold_reason=None) actually clears a previously set hold_reason. Run it on a task that was held and then re-claimed.
Log a notify line when head_sha fails at the claim, so a skipped derivation is visible.
Confirm in the spec that no existing log_run call runs on the non-JSON failed path, or name which one the test should expect.
State in the docstring that the registry status stays failed after a derived done or held write, and that B5 must key on status_reason, not the registry status.
